llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is most consistent with a hard WSS input-port failure in the ROADM at S06. S06 is the sole element common to every affected working path, and a failed WSS port can remove many channels simultaneously, producing the widespread OCH_LOS and downstream amplifier input-LOS alarms seen at onset.

proposals.rationale: A WSS input-port failure at S06 explains the common dependency, simultaneous multi-service outage, widespread OCH_LOS, and loss reaching multiple S06-originating optical sections. The unchanged S06 booster telemetry argues somewhat against an optical blockage before those boosters, but the overall fault scope strongly localizes to the S06 ROADM.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

proposals.rationale: A disconnected OMS input could directly cause AMP_INPUT_LOS at O1. It does not explain the simultaneous O2 alarm and network-wide set of affected channels without an additional failure, while upstream power telemetry reportedly did not change.

Severe added loss on the span feeding O1 could produce its input LOS. A single span fault cannot account for the concurrent loss on the separate S06-S21 section or all services sharing S06, and no supporting power change was recorded.

An S06 switch-fabric failure could interrupt many ODUs simultaneously. It is unlikely because it would generate ODU-layer failures rather than widespread optical OCH_LOS and amplifier input-LOS alarms.
